sources.entry: isort - A Python utility / library to sort imports.

summary.one_liner: isort is a Python utility and library that sorts imports alphabetically and separates them into sections by type, usable from the command line, from Python code, or via editor plugins and a Git pre-commit hook.
summary.what_it_does: Sorts Python import statements alphabetically and groups them into sections (for example standard library, third-party, and local). It wraps long "from" imports across lines according to a configurable multi-line output mode and line length, and can balance wrapped imports into a more even grid. A command-line tool can rewrite files or directories in place, show a diff without applying changes, or run in check-only mode (-c) to report incorrectly sorted files. A Python API offers isort.file() and isort.code() for sorting from code. Imports can be skipped per line or per file using "isort:skip" and "isort:skip_file" markers, and the README mentions a hook function for Git pre-commit scripts and official pre-commit support.
use_cases: sort imports in a Python project automatically
check code formatting of imports in CI or pre-commit
clean up import blocks before committing
sort imports from inside a Python script
notable: Balanced multi-line wrapping (balanced_wrapping option) that produces more even import grids
Check-only mode (-c) for verifying import order in CI or pre-commit hooks
Per-line and per-file skip markers (isort:skip, isort:skip_file)
Configurable sections, ordering, and 12 multi-line output modes
Can format Python 2 code although it runs on Python 3.11+
caveats: --atomic mode is disabled by default because it can prevent running on code written for a different Python version
Professional support is offered only through the Tidelift subscription
